themes.title: Trump-Meloni feud escalates ahead of NATO summit
themes.blurb: Right-wing media across the US, Italy, UK, Spain, and France are intensifying coverage of Donald Trump's latest attacks on Italian PM Giorgia Meloni, including a meme calling for a 'restraining order' against her. The feud has overshadowed the upcoming NATO summit in Ankara, with Italian officials downplaying the tensions while US outlets frame it as a transatlantic rift.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump's Truth Social posts mocking Meloni dominate US right-wing coverage, with outlets like Fox News and The Daily Beast amplifying the feud.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian media focus on Meloni's silence and ministers' dismissals of Trump's attacks, while right-wing outlets like Il Giornale frame it as a test of Italy's sovereignty.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: UK right-wing media, including GB News, highlight the feud as a distraction from NATO unity, with Farage-aligned commentators criticizing Meloni's 'submissive' stance.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Spanish right-wing outlets like ABC and OkDiario frame the feud as a clash of egos, with Vox leaders using it to criticize Spain's left-wing government for 'weakening' Europe.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: French right-wing media, including CNews, draw parallels to Le Pen's own transatlantic tensions, with commentators urging Meloni to stand firm against US pressure.

themes.title: Far-right AfD party congress sparks mass protests in Germany
themes.blurb: Germany's AfD party congress in Erfurt has become a flashpoint for cross-national right-wing coverage, with outlets in Germany, France, the UK, Italy, and Spain highlighting the party's radicalization and the unprecedented scale of protests. The event has reignited debates about far-right extremism and democratic resilience in Europe.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: German outlets like WELT and FAZ focus on AfD's internal power struggles, with Alice Weidel consolidating control and Björn Höcke's faction gaining influence.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: French right-wing media, including Le Figaro, draw parallels to RN's own challenges, with commentators warning about the normalization of far-right rhetoric.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: UK right-wing outlets like The Telegraph frame the protests as a sign of Germany's 'woke' establishment suppressing dissent, with Farage-aligned commentators praising AfD's 'anti-establishment' stance.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian right-wing media, including Il Giornale, highlight the protests as a warning against left-wing 'censorship,' with Salvini praising AfD's 'patriotic' policies.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Spanish right-wing outlets like ABC frame the protests as a 'globalist' attack on national sovereignty, with Vox leaders using it to criticize Spain's left-wing government.

themes.title: PP-Vox coalitions reshape Spain's regional governments
themes.blurb: Right-wing media in Spain, Italy, France, and Argentina are closely following the formation of PP-Vox coalition governments in Andalusia, Extremadura, Aragón, and Castilla y León. The alliances are framed as a blueprint for a future national right-wing government, with Vox's 'national priority' policies becoming a key point of contention.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Spanish right-wing outlets like ABC and OkDiario celebrate the coalitions as a victory for 'common sense,' with Vox leaders emphasizing their role in shaping conservative policies.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Partido Popular
countries.note: PP-aligned media, including El Mundo, frame the coalitions as a pragmatic necessity, with Feijóo downplaying Vox's influence while defending the alliances.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian right-wing media, including Il Giornale, highlight the coalitions as a model for Italy, with Meloni praising the 'responsible' approach of PP and Vox.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: French right-wing outlets like Le Figaro draw parallels to RN's own coalition strategies, with commentators urging Le Pen to adopt a similar 'pragmatic' approach.

countries.name: 🇦🇷 La Libertad Avanza
countries.note: Argentinian right-wing media, including Infobae, frame the coalitions as a sign of Europe's shift toward 'libertarian' policies, with Milei praising Vox's 'anti-globalist' stance.

themes.title: Marine Le Pen's eligibility ruling dominates French far-right
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right media in France, Spain, Italy, Germany, and the UK are intensively covering the upcoming Paris appeals court ruling on Marine Le Pen's eligibility for the 2027 presidential election. The verdict is framed as a defining moment for Europe's far-right, with Jordan Bardella positioned as Le Pen's potential successor.

countries.name: 🇫🇷 Rassemblement National
countries.note: French right-wing outlets like Le Figaro and CNews focus on the legal and political implications of the ruling, with RN leaders rallying behind Le Pen while preparing for Bardella's potential candidacy.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Spanish right-wing media, including ABC and OkDiario, frame the ruling as a test of judicial independence, with Vox leaders drawing parallels to their own legal battles.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Italian right-wing outlets like Il Giornale highlight the ruling as a sign of Europe's 'judicial activism,' with Meloni praising Le Pen's resilience.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: German right-wing media, including WELT, frame the ruling as a warning against 'political persecution,' with AfD leaders using it to criticize Germany's establishment.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: UK right-wing outlets like The Telegraph draw parallels to Farage's own legal challenges, with commentators praising Le Pen's 'anti-establishment' stance.

themes.title: Hungary's constitutional crisis under Péter Magyar
themes.blurb: Right-wing and far-right media in Hungary, Poland, Germany, and the UK are closely following the constitutional crisis in Hungary, with PM Péter Magyar's proposed amendments to remove President Tamás Sulyok and impose term limits sparking protests from Fidesz and international scrutiny. The crisis is framed as a power struggle between Magyar's reformist government and Orbán's legacy.

countries.name: 🇭🇺 Fidesz / Tisza
countries.note: Hungarian media outlets like Origo and Magyar Nemzet frame the crisis as a 'coup' against Orbán's legacy, with Fidesz leaders organizing protests and accusing Magyar of 'authoritarianism.'

countries.name: 🇵🇱 Prawo i Sprawiedliwość
countries.note: Polish right-wing media, including Do Rzeczy, highlight the crisis as a warning against 'liberal overreach,' with PiS leaders drawing parallels to Poland's own constitutional disputes.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: German right-wing outlets like FAZ frame the crisis as a sign of Hungary's 'democratic backsliding,' with AfD leaders using it to criticize the EU's 'interference' in national sovereignty.

countries.name: 🇬🇧 Reform UK
countries.note: UK right-wing media, including The Telegraph, highlight the crisis as a test of Hungary's commitment to 'Western values,' with Farage-aligned commentators praising Magyar's 'anti-establishment' stance.
